column1: # Wave B1 — every frame where (n-1)%3==1, each editing its own n-1 (a KIND-A frame).
# frame 2 was rendered in the B pilot and is already in the ledger; 118 rows here.
# `loc` is the location of the BASE frame, not the nominal scene map. The scene map's
# boundaries fall on B frames in several places (116, 128, 218...); a B frame cannot
# change location, so the scene actually turns at the next A frame. Base wins.
# Prompt built from this file (nothing else — no asset sheets, no style formula, no
# palette lock; adding any of them makes the model rebuild instead of edit):
#   Take the reference image and keep it EXACTLY: same composition, same crop, same
#   camera, same character, same colors, same background, same style. Change ONLY:
#   {change}. Do not redraw or re-stage anything else.
# Base beats for frames 97-355 come from EP01-waveA-beats.tsv. Base beats for frames
# 4-94 were never persisted and the CDN is blocked from this session's egress, so those
# changes were authored against the narration-to-frame mapping and the scene map rather
# than against the rendered image. They are phrased to be additive where the base
# staging is uncertain — if the named element is absent the model introduces it, which
# is still on-message and still a glance-visible change.

column4: change
the banknote in the frame has been torn in two, the larger half pulled away from the counter
three small SUIT silhouettes have appeared standing in a row behind the counter
each of the three SUIT silhouettes is now holding a small paper scrap
a small corner section has been cut out of the banknote and set aside on the ruled plane
the small corner scrap has been circled with a heavy inked ring
the till drawer has sprung open, standing empty
every noodle hand has been withdrawn from the counter, leaving it untouched
a dotted trail line now runs from the counter off toward the right edge of the frame
a row of open empty hands has appeared along the dotted trail across the ruled plane
the banknote at the end of the trail has shrunk to a bare sliver
the single block on the rail has separated into three blocks stacked one on top of another
a small plain clock face has appeared beside the rail, its hand just past the top
a card has been laid flat against the reader with a short contact line drawn between them
two plain labels have appeared beside the stack, one wide and one narrow
the card has lifted clear of the reader and the contact line is gone
the largest of the three blocks has slid forward well ahead of the other two
a small scrap has been cut from the large block and laid beside it
a blank nameplate has appeared on the wall above the desk
the nameplate has been underlined twice with heavy ink
the lending window behind the desk has been shuttered closed
a turnstile has appeared standing in the middle of the lobby floor
the stack of paper on the desk has slid a short way sideways and stopped
a single small scrap has peeled off the top of the stack and lifted into the air
a taut line now runs from the slab off to the left edge of the frame
a small meter box has been clamped onto the taut line
a small scrap has arrived at the near end of the rail
everything else has been cleared from the counter, leaving the white terminal alone
MARV has sat down on the sofa
a small paper scrap has appeared drifting down from the top of the frame
the drifting scrap has halved in size
an open noodle hand has entered from the right, palm up beneath the scrap
the plucked scrap is now pinched between two fingers and held up in front of MARV's face
THE SUIT has laid both noodle hands flat on the paper section
the cut is finished and the large cut-away portion has been lifted clear of the desk
the cut-away portion has vanished into the chute and that hand is now empty
a dotted outline has been inked around the empty space where the missing corner was
the dotted cut-lines now run the full width of the banknote, edge to edge
MARV has picked up a large pair of scissors in one noodle hand
a plain paper price tag now hangs from the front of the stack of sacks
the crate has been set down on the counter and THE BARISTA's arms hang empty at his sides
a lid has been placed on top of the lone paper cup
the paper strip has been lowered onto the counter and THE BARISTA is looking straight ahead
THE FARMER has straightened up and is standing upright among the rows
the woven basket is now full to the brim and the hand has withdrawn
THE FARMER has unpinned the scrap and is holding it out at arm's length
the queue behind THE FARMER has doubled in length, running off the right edge of the frame
every silhouette in the line is now carrying a paper scrap larger than THE FARMER's
the sack has travelled to the far end of the conveyor
every SUIT in the row is now holding a pinch and the sack has passed beyond them
the stack of stamped forms has grown taller than the sack
the pour has finished and THE BARISTA has set the cup down on the counter
the portafilter has been locked into the espresso machine and the hands are gone
the taped paper section has been torn away, leaving only two short strips of tape
THE LANDLORD's feet have come off the desk and he is sitting upright
the paper section has gone into a drawer and the desk is bare again
a second paper section has slid under the door on top of the first
a measuring bracket has been inked above each of the two strips
MARV has stood up and is pointing at the large strip
a single LANDLORD silhouette has appeared standing on the large strip
a heavy arrow has been inked pointing down at the tiny strip
the drip from the pipe has become a puddle spreading across the floor
the repair figure has stood up and is holding the invoice out at arm's length
the six torn pieces are now spread apart in a row across the counter
four of the five sections have been slid off to the left, leaving one behind
the small scrap has been circled with a heavy inked ring
MARV has picked the scrap up and is holding it flat on his palm
the coins have been set down on the counter in one short stack
the last cup has been cleared and the counter is completely bare
a heavy bracket has been inked around the whole exploded diagram
the smallest section has been lifted onto its edge, standing upright
MARV has stopped at the far end of the diagram and turned to face it
a dividing line has been inked down the floor between the two queues
one heavy horizontal rule has been drawn across the middle of the menu board
both hands have been withdrawn and the card and the banknote are both gone
both figures have turned away from the counter, each carrying a cup
the cloth is gone and THE BARISTA has stepped back from the menu board
the tiny extra mark has been boxed in with a heavy inked square
one banknote has been labelled with a small card shape and the other with a small coin shape
both cut-away pieces have been moved to the same side of the ruled plane
the returned scrap has been pressed flat onto its note and the other note is bare
the empty open hand has closed into a fist
the arrow between the two figures has thickened and doubled in length
every arrow has been redrawn tilting upward toward the top right corner
the vault door has swung open at the end of the arrows
one group of tally marks on the chalkboard has been circled
the neat stack of paper sheets has been fanned out across the desk
the arrows have all merged into one single thick arrow at the vault door
the mailbox has tipped over and the scraps have spilled toward the large house
the largest house at the right end has grown taller than the top of the frame
every arrow along the row of houses has doubled in thickness
a single small scrap is now leaving through the door of the smallest house
the figure's pocket is now empty and turned inside out
the full pocket has burst and scraps are spilling out down the side
one thin seam line has appeared running the full height of the slab
one chair has been pulled out from the desk, still empty
the switch has flipped over to its other position
MARV has tilted his head back to look straight up the slab
the banknote hand has dropped to the table and only the card is still raised
the wallet has snapped shut with the card lying on top of it
a dotted line has been drawn around both queues, enclosing them together
MARV has lowered the card face down onto his knee
the small door has swung shut while the vault stays open
the tiny shape has been dropped and only the enormous one is still held up
MARV has picked up a pen and is holding it over the open page
the pen has been set down beside the notebook and the line is finished
MARV has leaned forward toward the empty chair
the chair has been turned around to face away from the camera
MARV's thumb has lifted clear of the card terminal
the hand has withdrawn, leaving the cup standing alone on the counter
the dotted cut-lines on every fixture have darkened into solid heavy outlines
MARV has picked the cup up off the counter
the floating scrap has sunk halfway below the surface of the coffee
the scrap is now clear of the mug, held dripping above it
a faint dotted outline of the scrap's original larger size has been drawn around it
the thin sliver has been reduced to a single short dash
a bracket has been drawn spanning the gap between the two marks
MARV has raised one noodle arm to point into the gap
the red margin line has thinned to a single faint hairline at the frame edge
